title: Wave speed
target: Use speed, frequency and wavelength in a consistent relationship.
criteria: Check frequency and wavelength changes at fixed speed.
Distinguish medium speed from oscillation rate.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A wave has frequency 6 Hz and wavelength 0.75 m. What is speed?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A wave moves at 18 m/s with wavelength 60 cm. What is frequency?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A medium keeps wave speed fixed. Frequency rises from 5 Hz to 15 Hz. What happens to wavelength?
cpa.guide: λ = v/f; tripling f at fixed v divides wavelength by 3.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: At fixed speed, wavelength changes from 2.4 m to 1.2 m. How does frequency change?
cpa.guide: Halving wavelength requires doubled frequency to keep fλ fixed.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A string point moves up and down while a pulse travels right. Which distinction is correct?
options: The point’s oscillation and the wave’s propagation describe different motions.
A transverse wave cannot carry energy.
The point’s maximum upward speed always equals wave speed.
The string point must travel right with the pulse.
cpa.guide: Local material motion need not follow the propagation direction or speed.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A driver is adjusted to oscillate faster while string tension and mass per length remain fixed. In the ideal string model, what changes?
options: Propagation speed must increase by the same factor.
Frequency stays fixed and only amplitude can change.
Frequency increases and wavelength decreases; propagation speed stays fixed.
Every string particle flows toward the far end.
cpa.guide: The medium sets speed in this model; v = fλ requires a compensating wavelength change.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
